name: Language Models can Solve Computer Tasks
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces recursive criticism and improvement prompting for language-model agents performing computer tasks, evaluated on MiniWoB++ with a small number of demonstrations per task.

name: AdaPlanner: Adaptive Planning from Feedback with Language Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. This is a general planning framework; MiniWoB++ supplies the interface-agent evidence, while ALFWorld is a separate environment.
summary: Introduces AdaPlanner, which revises code-structured plans in response to environmental feedback and reuses successful plans as exemplars. Experiments include MiniWoB++ web tasks alongside ALFWorld.

name: A Zero-Shot Language Agent for Computer Control with Structured Reflection
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies a zero-shot computer-control agent that plans executable actions and organizes its own reflections after mistakes. MiniWoB++ experiments examine learning to complete tasks without supplied expert trajectories.

name: On the Multi-turn Instruction Following for Conversational Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: MT-Mind2Web evaluates web navigation through sequences of conversational user instructions. Self-MAP combines memory-augmented planning with reflection to preserve context and dependencies across those interaction turns.

name: SheetAgent: Towards A Generalist Agent for Spreadsheet Reasoning and Manipulation via Large Language Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces SheetRM, a benchmark of long-horizon spreadsheet tasks, and SheetAgent, an LLM agent that plans, retrieves information and reflects while manipulating spreadsheets.

name: VLM Agents Generate Their Own Memories: Distilling Experience into Embodied Programs of Thought
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v6). VisualWebArena is one of several evaluation settings for this general VLM-agent method.
summary: ICAL turns imperfect agent trajectories into reusable strategies and action annotations through reflection and human feedback, with VisualWebArena among its evaluations.

name: Agent Q: Advanced Reasoning and Learning for Autonomous AI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract evaluates it in WebShop and booking scenarios.
summary: Agent Q combines guided tree search, self-critique and preference-based fine-tuning to train web agents from successful and unsuccessful interactions.

name: ExACT: Teaching AI Agents to Explore with Reflective-MCTS and Exploratory Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v5). The reported agent evaluation is on VisualWebArena.
summary: ExACT combines reflective tree search with learning from search experience to help web agents explore, assess states and backtrack on VisualWebArena.

name: From Novice to Expert: LLM Agent Policy Optimization via Step-wise Reinforcement Learning
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot. Official full-paper experimental sections explicitly evaluate WebShop and Mind2Web; the overall optimization method also covers embodied and question-answering tasks.
summary: Introduces StepAgent, which compares agent and expert actions to supply intermediate rewards for policy learning, with implicit-reward and inverse-RL variants. Evaluation includes WebShop and Mind2Web alongside non-web tasks.

name: R2D2: Remembering, Replaying and Dynamic Decision Making with a Reflective Agentic Memory
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The abstract evaluates R2D2 on WebArena.
summary: R2D2 gives web agents a replay-buffer map of visited pages and a reflection step for analyzing errors and revising navigation strategies.

name: Guiding VLM Agents with Process Rewards at Inference Time for GUI Navigation
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.
summary: Guides visual GUI agents at inference time with a process-reward model that evaluates intermediate actions. It combines stepwise guidance with trajectory reflection and retry mechanisms in static and interactive navigation tasks.

name: WebCoT: Enhancing Web Agent Reasoning by Reconstructing Chain-of-Thought in Reflection, Branching, and Rollback
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: WebCoT turns reflection, look-ahead, branching and rollback procedures into chain-of-thought training rationales. Fine-tuning on these reconstructed trajectories is evaluated for web-agent self-improvement and transfer across navigation tasks.

name: Training LLM-Based Agents with Synthetic Self-Reflected Trajectories and Partial Masking
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). WebShop is one evaluation task alongside ALFWorld and SciWorld.
summary: Introduces STeP, which trains agents on synthetic trajectories containing error reflections and corrections while masking poor steps; WebShop is one of three evaluated tasks.

name: UI-Evol: Automatic Knowledge Evolving for Computer Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces UI-Evol, which extracts action sequences from agent interactions and critiques external guidance against those traces. Evaluation on OSWorld examines how revised operational knowledge affects execution and behavioral consistency.

name: Let's Think in Two Steps: Mitigating Agreement Bias in MLLMs with Self-Grounded Verification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The verifier study also covers robotics, beyond web and computer-use agents.
summary: Studies agreement bias in multimodal agent verifiers across web navigation and computer use, and introduces SGV to assess trajectories using self-generated priors.

name: MobileUse: A GUI Agent with Hierarchical Reflection for Autonomous Mobile Operation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: MobileUse reflects on errors at action and task timescales, invoking reflection when needed and using proactive exploration to learn unfamiliar apps. It evaluates this mobile execution framework on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab and describes a toolkit for physical-device operation.

name: Instruction Agent: Enhancing Agent with Expert Demonstration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its reported success rate concerns a selected set of OSWorld tasks that other top-ranked agents failed.
summary: Introduces Instruction Agent, a GUI agent that follows instructions extracted from one expert demonstration and uses verification and backtracking to handle interruptions.

name: Mano Technical Report
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The abstract reports evaluation on GUI benchmarks including Mind2Web and OSWorld.
summary: Introduces Mano, a GUI agent trained with simulated data, supervised fine-tuning, and offline and online RL, with a verification module for error recovery.

name: D-Artemis: A Deliberative Cognitive Framework for Mobile GUI Multi-Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces D-Artemis, a mobile GUI agent framework that retrieves app-specific tips, checks actions before execution, and reflects on their outcomes without trajectory training.

name: WebGen-Agent: Enhancing Interactive Website Generation with Multi-Level Feedback and Step-Level Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GUI agents provide testing feedback for generated websites; WebGen-Agent itself generates website code.
summary: Introduces WebGen-Agent for website code generation, using screenshot critiques and GUI-agent tests to refine code and provide step-level training rewards.

name: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Distills generalizable reasoning strategies from both successful and failed agent trajectories into a persistent memory bank for test-time retrieval.

name: History-Aware Reasoning for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: HAR-GUI combines episodic reasoning and short-term memory to use earlier interactions when selecting GUI actions. Its training constructs reflective scenarios and correction guidance and applies a hybrid reinforcement-learning reward to the 3B policy.

name: "Are We Done Yet?": A Vision-Based Judge for Autonomous Task Completion of Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: This study tests vision-language models as task-completion judges using screenshots and instructions from 42 built-in macOS applications. It evaluates judgment accuracy on human-labeled tasks and separately studies how judge feedback affects agent task success.

name: GAIR: GUI Automation via Information-Joint Reasoning and Group Reflection
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces GAIR, which combines information from specialized GUI models through a general-purpose coordinating model. When the available information is insufficient, group reflection sends targeted requests back to the specialists before selecting an operation.

name: SmartSnap: Proactive Evidence Seeking for Self-Verifying Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: SmartSnap trains GUI agents to collect concise screenshot evidence of task completion for an LLM judge, with experiments on mobile tasks.

name: GUITester: Enabling GUI Agents for Exploratory Defect Discovery
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces GUITestBench for interactive defect discovery and GUITester, which separates task navigation from anomaly verification. Testing-oriented plans and history-based reflection help distinguish software defects from agent execution mistakes.

name: OS-Symphony: A Holistic Framework for Robust and Generalist Computer-Using Agent
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: OS-Symphony coordinates milestone-based reflection and memory with tools that build visually aligned tutorials through browser interaction. The framework evaluates trajectory correction and adaptation on online computer-use benchmarks including OSWorld.

name: EvoCUA: Evolving Computer Use Agents via Learning from Scalable Synthetic Experience
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: EvoCUA combines task synthesis with executable validators, asynchronous sandbox rollouts and iterative policy updates. It turns successful routines and analyzed failures into supervision and evaluates the evolving agent on OSWorld.

name: Do Multi-Agents Dream of Electric Screens? Achieving Perfect Accuracy on AndroidWorld Through Task Decomposition
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported task-success result is on the AndroidWorld benchmark.
summary: Minitap coordinates six specialized agents for AndroidWorld tasks, checking text input against device state and detecting action loops to revise its strategy.

name: OpAgent: Operator Agent for Web Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: OpAgent combines multi-task GUI fine-tuning with online web reinforcement learning using outcome judgments and rule-based progress rewards. A modular planner, grounder, reflector and summarizer support navigation and recovery, evaluated separately from the underlying trained policy.

name: World-Model-Augmented Web Agents with Action Correction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: WAC has a web-agent action model consult a world model, simulate action outcomes and use judge feedback to correct actions before execution.

name: GUI-CEval: A Hierarchical and Comprehensive Chinese Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUI-CEval evaluates Chinese mobile GUI agents through a hierarchy of atomic abilities and application-level tasks collected on physical devices. Its diagnostics cover perception, planning, reflection, execution and post-action evaluation across a broad set of apps.

name: CAPTCHA Solving for Native GUI Agents: Automated Reasoning-Action Data Generation and Self-Corrective Training
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces ReCAP, a native GUI agent for interactive CAPTCHA challenges, trained with generated interaction trajectories, reasoning traces and self-correction data.

name: Measure Twice, Click Once: Co-evolving Proposer and Visual Critic via Reinforcement Learning for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Trains a GUI grounding proposer together with a visual critic that evaluates candidate locations rendered on screenshots. An adaptive reinforcement-learning schedule balances their development, using proposal diversity and critic feedback during training.

name: VLAA-GUI: Knowing When to Stop, Recover, and Search, A Modular Framework for GUI Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: VLAA-GUI combines mandatory checks for visually supported completion, multi-tier loop recovery and on-demand workflow search. Optional coding and grounding agents support execution, with component ablations on Linux and Windows GUI tasks.

name: DRIVE: Modeling Skills at the Reasoning and Interaction Levels for Web Agents under Continual Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: DRIVE separates reusable reasoning skills from page-specific interaction skills for web agents, retrieving both to plan tasks and execute actions on websites.

name: Learning to Adapt: Self-Improving Web Agent via Cognitive-Aware Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces SCALE, which uses exploration roles and graph planning to train web agents, and SCALE-20k, a dataset of tasks and demonstrations from real websites.

name: Learning from Failure: Inference-Time Self-Improvement for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Uses failed computer-use trajectories to diagnose failure modes and generate inference-time agent code patches, with light human verification. An OSWorld study evaluates this failure-driven improvement loop without additional model training.

name: BaRA: Budget-constrained and Reliable Web Data Collection Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Its focus is site-level data collection within an interaction budget.
summary: Introduces BaRA, a web data-collection agent that discovers live site links, checks extracted text, images, and videos, and uses history to recover from failures.

name: Falsifiable Commitment Planning for Self-Correcting Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces FCPAgent, which attaches confirming and falsifying evidence to each skill-grounded plan step. A plan–test–repair loop checks actions and observations, then localizes contradictions so execution, skills, or plans can be revised at the appropriate level.

name: MemHarness: Memory Is Reconstructed, Not Replayed
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The method is evaluated on ALFWorld and WebShop, so web operation is only one evaluation setting.
summary: Introduces MemHarness, which trains agents to critique and reconstruct retrieved experience before acting; WebShop is one of two evaluation environments.

name: CUADebug: Diagnosing and Repairing Computer-Use Agent Failures
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: CUADebug combines a failure taxonomy and human-annotated OSWorld failure trajectories with an agent that locates causal steps and proposes corrections from screenshots and action traces. It evaluates root-cause diagnosis separately from controlled task re-execution and failure recovery.

name: StepReflect: Structured UI Transition Reflection for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: StepReflect predicts structured per-action reflections from transition specifications and paired visual evidence. The paper distinguishes offline transition-label accuracy from online task success when the reflection model is integrated into mobile agents.

name: AndroidReality: How Far Are Mobile Agents from the Real World?
notes: The reviewed protocol normally activates one perturbation type at a time while preserving task semantics and reward. Basis: complete retained abstract and source-reviewed sections of the exact-version paper (3.1 Perturbation formulation; 3.2 Injection; 3.3 Evaluation protocol; 4.3 Error analysis).
summary: Extends AndroidWorld with controlled state, transition, and action perturbations to test mobile-agent robustness, and studies a training-free introspective recovery mechanism.

name: LookAgain: Closed-Loop GUI Grounding with Visually Grounded Reflection
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: LookAgain treats a GUI coordinate as a revisable hypothesis, rendering its marker and a local screenshot patch before confirmation. Reflective supervised trajectories provide a cold start, followed by GRPO using terminal grounding correctness.

name: Test-Time Self-Evolving GUI Visual Grounding via Reflection-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces a Test-Time Self-Evolving framework for GUI grounding that explores unseen interfaces, reflects on predicted coordinates, and distills those reflections into the model.

name: Reflection with Action-Induced Visual Differences for Desktop GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Evidence-First Reflection, which separates extraction of action-induced screen changes from judgment of whether an operation achieved its objective. It filters visual differences into relevant evidence before a desktop agent’s reflector decides how execution should continue.

name: AnchorGUI: Asymmetric Memory for Dual-Scale Learning in GUI Navigation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AnchorGUI compares expected and observed UI transitions and selectively retains screenshots when they disagree. This asymmetric memory supports immediate correction and focuses cross-attempt experience distillation on likely failure steps.

name: Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: EvoSkill-GUI revises reusable skill files from execution feedback through an executor–critic loop. It studies how training-free updates to localization, recovery and procedure information help subsequent mobile and desktop tasks.

name: When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows
notes: The mobile evaluation uses text UI observations and one fixed instance for each of 116 AndroidWorld task types; three repeats share seed 0. Five agent families use different budgets, with candidate-interface and tool-call granularity changes in some variants. Reported costs use fixed experimental prices, and outcome-selected trace labels are not population failure rates. Faster selection does not imply faster or more reliable task completion.
summary: Evaluates Jev as a bounded action selector inside three AndroidWorld agents and two text-based ALFWorld agents, separating decision savings from task success, recovery and resources per delivered outcome.

name: Step-Aligned Script Generation with Verification and Recovery for Web Automation Testing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports evaluation on three public web benchmarks.

name: AdaGround: Token-Normalized Adaptive Zooming with Verifier-in-the-Loop Refinement for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported evaluations use Qwen3-VL models on OSWorld-G, ScreenSpot-Pro, and UI-Vision.
summary: Introduces AdaGround, a training-free GUI grounding method that adjusts screenshot zoom to target size and uses a click verifier to refine or reject predictions.

name: MAGAR: Multimodal Agents for GUI-Based 3D Mechanical Assembly and Minimal Rework
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported results use recorded states from held-out assembly families.
summary: Introduces MAGAR-Bench for GUI-based 3D mechanical assembly decisions and recovery, and MAGAR, a selective correction method for assembly outputs and actions.

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces ScienceCUA, which turns scientific software documentation into reusable agent skills and revises them using execution feedback, with two audited evaluation variants.

name: LongHorizonUI
notes: Code release of the ICLR 2026 paper "LongHorizonUI: A Unified Framework for Robust long-horizon Task Automation of GUI Agent" (the repository description says ICLR2026; the README cites it with anonymous authors and no link). Each screenshot passes through RapidOCR, the OmniParser v2 YOLO icon detector (downloaded from microsoft/OmniParser-v2.0 on first use) and template matching when an icon template directory is set; the merged elements are drawn as numbered boxes, and that annotated screenshot with a step prompt is what the Gemini, Azure OpenAI or OpenAI model receives. Actions are click, long press, swipe, drag, text input and key press. With the fallback cascade on (the default), an element-index target that fails is retried as a relative point inside the box and then as absolute coordinates with jitter; a progress monitor can roll back to the last committed snapshot, at most three times per task. The README documents only the offline mode, which replays a task's recorded screenshot sequence with either the task description or step-by-step instructions. run.py also has a live subcommand that lists USB-connected devices, but at the reviewed commit AndroidContext never opens a device connection (its context stays None), so device actions return without acting. The repository also has a Gradio app, agents that turn recorded taps and swipes into step descriptions, a scrcpy-based Android recording tool, step-level evaluation scripts and the project page source. The LongGUIBench dataset is not released (the README link is a placeholder), the requirements.txt the README installs from is not in the tree, and the README's Apache-2.0 badge and LICENSE link are not backed by a license file. Not a fork, not archived; no release. Code was read, not run.
summary: Code for the LongHorizonUI Android agent: OCR plus OmniParser icon detection yields numbered element boxes for an LLM, and failed taps fall back from element index to relative and absolute points with rollback.

name: Roubao
notes: Kotlin Android app (minimum SDK 26) published by Turbo1123. Shizuku gives it ADB-level shell access without root, which DeviceController.kt uses for screencap, input tap/swipe/text and am start; the agent's floating overlay is hidden while each plain screenshot is taken. In the default mode MobileAgent.kt runs Manager (plan), Executor (one of click, double_tap, long_press, type, swipe, system_button, open_app, wait, take_over or answer, with pixel coordinates), ActionReflector (compares the before and after screenshots) and an optional Notetaker over an OpenAI-compatible VLM API, for at most 25 steps by default; the README calls this layer a Kotlin port of Mobile-Agent-v3. Two other modes call GUI-Owl through Alibaba Cloud DashScope's GUI agent endpoint (default model pre-gui_owl_7b), which returns actions directly, or an OpenAI-compatible MAI-UI server (default localhost:8000, MAI-UI-2B) with MAI-UI's prompt format and up to three history screenshots. A Skills layer (app/src/main/assets/skills.json) can instead hand a request to another app through a deep link, and Tools cover app search, deep links, clipboard, shell and HTTP. When screencap is blocked on a secure screen the agent asks the user before continuing; the Manager prompt stops the run when a screen actively asks for payment confirmation, a password or biometric verification, and the Executor can hand logins and captchas to the user (take_over) or ask for confirmation of payment actions. The README says a 2.0 version based on AccessibilityService is developed on a separate branch; this record describes main. Root LICENSE is MIT; not a fork, not archived; latest release V1.4.2. Code was read, not run.
summary: On-device Android phone agent in Kotlin that captures screenshots and taps, swipes and types through Shizuku without a PC, running a planner, executor and reflector loop on any OpenAI-compatible VLM, GUI-Owl or MAI-UI.

name: LongHorizonUI: A Unified Framework for Robust long-horizon Task Automation of GUI Agent
notes: Reviewed against the ICLR 2026 proceedings page and PDF; the OpenReview forum lists it as an ICLR 2026 Poster. Experiments were not reproduced. LongHorizonUI's components run without fine-tuning, with Gemini 2.5 Pro as the default backbone; Appendix D.6 also reports Gemini 1.5 Flash and Qwen2.5-VL-7B backbones. LongGUIBench tasks need more than 15 steps across games and general apps; the paper states 371 scenarios but gives 207 game scenarios in Section 2.1 and 224 in Appendix D.2, and does not name the benchmark's device platform. Other reported evaluations are ScreenSpot grounding, AndroidControl and GUI-Odyssey, plus zero-shot AndroidWorld and OSWorld runs in Appendix D.5. The paper points to kane2kang.github.io/LongHorizonUI for code, which was not reviewed here. No arXiv version was found.

The page states that the agent targets phones, in-car systems, TVs and PCs, names no mobile operating system, and lists usage as free for a limited time. The X-PLUG/MobileAgent README links this page as a limited-time free Mobile-Agent-v3 API; the page itself names no paper or released checkpoint, so no relation to the Mobile-Agent or GUI-Owl records is asserted.
